I rewrote the proposal and logged it as "rewrote" in `flags.jsonl`. Nobody currently owns this brief, so I edited it directly. I didn't open any page or screenshot.

`text-check.mjs` flagged nothing. I made two changes to `test-health/requirements.md`:
- **Title:** it now reads "Test health: are the tests real, and do they run?". The "you are a mastermind, on Sonnet" note moved to its own line under the title.
- **Steps:** the five "Do" steps are now `- [ ]` checkboxes, headed "tick each when done", so progress shows as ticks.

I left one thing alone: "3b1fae8d3" in "Known so far" is a bare commit hash that isn't linked.

The verdict is **fix**: the new way to run the browser tests works, but the doc reports results that no recorded run backs up, and part of it is out of date. This change touches no page, so there were no screenshots and the review covers only Requirements and Words. I made no code edits.

**What the work does well**
- One command, `TestRunner.mjs --browser`, now runs all 32 browser scripts. Each script on the list is marked pass, red (known failing) or skip.
- `run-all.mjs` runs the whole suite and adds one dated line to `run-all.jsonl` per run.
- Slow tests get their own time limit in `timeouts.json`.
- No locked code was edited, and the readme links every new file.

**Must change**
1. **Numbers with no run behind them.** `health.md` says the first run had 19 pass and 13 red. The only recorded run, in `run-all.jsonl`, was against the worktree's site: 16 passed, three scripts that must pass failed, and the result is a fail.
2. **Stale node failures.** The doc still says `Files.move.test.mjs` only times out. Its latest run fails with a permission error (`EPERM`) at 64 s. `ChatV2.test.mjs` and `ChatV3.test.mjs` are failing too, and the doc doesn't mention them.
3. **Dictate failures not passed on.** The doc says they went to the Dictate owner, but I found no message to mastermind-dictation-v3 or entry in `ux/Dictate/improvements.jsonl`. The Refine failures are filed properly.
4. **A fresh agent can't pick this up.** Commit 53047e744 sits on `worktree/test-browser`, not merged, and no log line says so. The checkboxes in `requirements.md` are all unticked.

**Worth a look**
- Two fields in the script list are never read by the runner: `kind:"node"` and `env`.
- Each run leaves a temp screenshots folder behind.
- On a timeout, only the node script is stopped, so a headless Chromium can keep running.
- `health.md` copies the reason for each failing script word for word from the script list.
- `run-all.jsonl` is committed and grows with every run.

The full report is at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/test-health/review.md`.

My verdict is **fix**: the work is mostly done, but one number in the health report has no record behind it, and three other gaps need closing before it merges. The report is at `public/framework/ai/sessions/2026/10/20/session-e00f55c9/test-health/review.md`. This change touches no page, so I answered only the Requirements and Words sections.

**What was asked and what landed:**
- **Done:** every test is listed, and the browser scripts that nothing used to run now have one command, `TestRunner.mjs --browser`. There is also a command that runs everything (`run-all.mjs`), plus per-file time limits. The readme links all of it.
- **Partly done:** the full run happened, but only against the test-browser worktree's own site, not the main site the brief asked for.

**Fixes:**
1. **The "19 pass" line in `health.md` isn't backed by any record.** `results.jsonl` has one browser line per script, and `dictation-bar`, `docs-tab` and `refresh` are failures there, so the record shows 16 pass. Either re-run from the main checkout or write 16.
2. **`health.md:15` is out of date.** It still says `Files.move.test.mjs` "passes but needs 86 s", while a line further down says it now fails with a permission error (`EPERM`). That failure should be filed in `Server/improvements.jsonl`.
3. **`ChatV2.test.mjs` and `ChatV3.test.mjs` fail with no cause found.** They were also never sent to mastermind-chat-model, which the brief's fence rule asks for.
4. **A fresh agent can't tell where this task stands.** The brief's checkboxes are all unticked, and no log line says the worktree is ready to merge or what is left.

**Notes:**
- The Dictate failures did reach their owner: commit b4dfb5639 logged them in the dictation-v3 session. `health.md` should link that line.
- `health.md` copies every failure reason from `browser-scripts.mjs`, so the two copies will drift apart.
- The new `--browser` path and the per-file time limits have no tests of their own.
- `--browser` assumes Playwright is installed globally and doesn't say so when it isn't.
- When a script times out, only the node process is killed, so on Windows its headless Chromium can keep running. That matters for an unattended nightly run.

I reviewed the test-health work and the verdict is **fix**. The code itself is sound, but most of last round's review findings are still open in the latest commit. The report is in `test-health/review.md`, in the same folder as the brief.

**What works:**
- There is now one command for the browser tests: `TestRunner.mjs --browser`.
- Each browser test has a status: must pass, known failing, or never run.
- `run-all.mjs` runs everything and appends a dated line to `run-all.jsonl`.
- Slow tests get their own time limit in `timeouts.json`.
- The readme links all four new files. I found no simpler design.

**What must change (4 fixes):**
1. **The "19 pass" claim has no record behind it.** In the results log of both checkouts, the most recent result for each browser test gives 16 passing. Three tests marked "must pass" (`dictation-bar`, `docs-tab`, `refresh`) only have failing lines.
2. **`health.md` contradicts itself on `Files.move.test.mjs`.** The table says it passes but times out; the new note says it now fails with a permission error (`EPERM`). That failure isn't filed in `Server/improvements.jsonl` either.
3. **The failing tests weren't sent to their owners.** The brief says to send them: the 8 new Dictate failures to the dictation-v3 mastermind, and the `ChatV2`/`ChatV3` failures to the chat-model mastermind. There is no record of either.
4. **A fresh agent couldn't continue from the folder.** The task log ends on a failed review and "session resumed". Nothing says that commit `ca0f9ddea` on the `worktree/test-browser` branch is waiting to be merged, and every checkbox in the brief is still unticked.

The report also has four smaller notes. One is that `health.md`'s "run everything" section still names only `TestRunner.mjs` instead of `run-all.mjs`.
